text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered: private-vpc-controlplane-connectivity for customer=Acme Retail (acme-retail-prod). PD INC-48291. Symptom: control plane heartbeats dropping for on-prem agents in us-east-1. Heartbeat rate ~0-5% since 02:14 UTC. Initial alert threshold crossed: 30m of missing heartbeats. Paging eng-oncall + netops + customer-success.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-48291 acknowledged by Maya S at 02:15:12 UTC.

Maya S: ack - I'm taking lead. grabbing control-plane leader logs and agent heartbeat metrics. @Tom (NetOps) can you check any BGP/peering churn to the customer's transit in us-east-1?

Tom (NetOps): looking. pulling BGP session history now. quick note: I see repeated BGP flaps from their ASN to our transit between 02:08-02:13 UTC — multiple route withdraws for their /24s. grabbing MRT and flow logs. pinging their infra contact.

Alex R: copying agent heartbeat dump for the last 25m (filtered):
```
{"agent_id":"acme-ec2-12","last_heartbeat":"2026-03-14T02:09:48Z","status":"stalled"}
{"agent_id":"acme-edge-3","last_heartbeat":"2026-03-14T02:11:02Z","status":"stalled"}
{"agent_id":"acme-edge-7","last_heartbeat":"2026-03-14T02:05:36Z","status":"stalled"}
```
Also seeing control-plane API error 502s in the same window.

Priya K: re: mitigation - we can enable hosted-control-plane-fallback for acme-retail-prod to restore management connectivity for agents while NetOps investigates. I can flip the route policy if we confirm it's safe. This is reversible and should be zero-downtime for inference traffic (only control plane routes change).

Maya S: do it. mark as temporary mitigation. Priya, run the following (I prepared a short runbook):
```
# enable hosted fallback for acme-retail-prod
redwoodctl routes set --account acme-retail-prod --controlplane fallback-hosted --confirm
# verify agent reconnections
redwoodctl agents list --account acme-retail-prod --status connected | grep acme
```
Make sure to keep TTL for fallback low so we can revert.

Priya K: running now.

Priya K: done at 02:20:03 UTC. agents starting to reconnect — seeing ~18/34 report back as connected within 90s. continuing to monitor. :thumbsup:

Tom (NetOps): update from BGP side: customer's transit engineer confirmed they pushed a firewall ACL change at ~02:07 UTC that accidentally dropped TCP 500/4500 and BGP session refresh trafic between our peer. They've rolled back the ACL at 02:22 UTC. I see BGP sessions stable again and routes re-announced.

Maya S: good. can we correlate agent reconnect times to the rollback? Alex, can you plot heartbeats per-agent?

Alex R: quick histogram: heartbeats recovered starting 02:21:30 -> 02:24:00. by 02:26 UTC, 32/34 agents show OK. attaching sample broker log snippet that shows session re-establishment:
```
[02:22:18Z] control-plane: session acme-edge-3 accepted, kv-sync ok
[02:22:19Z] control-plane: agent acme-edge-7 heartbeat=ok
```

Sam N: customer side says they did not schedule a maintenance but their network team confirms an emergency ACL rollback at 02:22. CS (Jane) is on the call with the customer's infra lead to confirm root cause and get RCA commitment.

Jane (Customer Success): ping from customer: they confirm an ACL change on a transit firewall was deployed inadvertently during a config push. they've opened an internal postmortem and will share timeline. They asked if there was any inference downtime — we should confirm service impact.

Maya S: impact summary so far: control-plane management plane degraded for ~13 minutes (02:09 - ~02:22); agent heartbeats partially restored by 02:26. No evidence that inference data plane (token generation) was impacted — models continued serving for requests routed to healthy nodes. However, control ops that require agent reconfiguration or new rollouts would have failed during the window. Marking customer-impact: partial management-plane outage, severity P2 (customer-facing but no customer-visible request failures reported yet).

Tom (NetOps): final from netops: BGP stable, routes present, no packet loss observed post-02:23 on monitored transit links. recommend follow-up: ask customer to add ACL change gating / change review to prevent accidental blocks, and add alerting on BGP session flaps per-customer.

Maya S: actions and owners:
- short: Priya enabled hosted-control-plane fallback to restore agent connectivity (done)
- netops (Tom) to coordinate with customer on ACL rollback confirmation and share MRT (done)
- eng/reliability (Alex) to collect logs and validate no config drift (in progress)
- cs (Jane) to confirm customer impact statement and timeline (in progress)
- ops (Sam) to create post-incident ticket and schedule postmortem (owner: Sam)

Sam N: created INC-48291-postmortem ticket in ops board, linking PD incident. assigned to Sam N, Tom, Alex. tentative postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

Maya S: lowering pager noise: short-term tuning - reduce alert window from 30m->15m for this specific heartbeat metric for private VPC accounts, and add a runbook link in the alert. Sam, please file change request.

Priya K: will revert hosted fallback once we get confirmation from Tom + Alex that agents are stable for 30m. planning revert at 03:00 UTC if stable.

Tom (NetOps): confirm revert is safe from network side.

Alex R: stability check at 02:55: all agents OK, no API 502s.

Priya K: reverted fallback at 03:03 UTC and agents remained connected.

Maya S: closing notes: incident resolved — control-plane heartbeats recovered after customer ACL rollback + temporary fallback. Impact: management-plane only, partial, no inference downtime observed. Postmortem owners: Sam N (ops), Tom (netops), Alex R (eng).

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident INC-48291 resolved at 03:10:07 UTC (duration ~55m).

Sam N: I'll draft blameless postmortem and include recommended alert tuning + automation to auto-failover to hosted control plane for future identical symptoms.

Maya S: thanks team. leaving final notes here and closing thread when postmortem ticket is created. :white_check_mark:
